sentences.text: Pachyrhinosaurus is a genus containing three distinct species of ceratopsian dinosaurs.
The genus was formally described and named by Charles M. Sternberg in the year 1950.

Rather than projecting horns, the skull features a massive, flattened protuberance on the nose alongside convex and concave bumps and unicorn-style horns located on the parietal bone just behind the eyes.
In 2024, a specimen nicknamed 'Big Sam' was unearthed at Pipestone Creek, measuring 138 centimeters in length with a nasal boss diameter of 43 centimeters.
One skull known as 'Harvey' displayed a massive lesion 195 millimeters wide on its right face that likely caused blindness in that eye.
Despite its robust appearance, the animal may have been capable of running at speeds reaching 9 meters per second, or approximately 32 kilometers per hour.
The initial examples of this dinosaur were discovered by Charles M. Sternberg in Alberta, Canada, during the year 1946.
The holotype and paratype skulls of the species P. canadensis were collected from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta between 1945 and 1946.
A significant bonebed was later found in 1974 by Al Lakusta along Pipestone Creek in Alberta.
This herbivore possessed strong cheek teeth batteries designed for cutting tough, fibrous plants and utilized a sharp beak to process its food.
The nasal boss of the species P. perotorum bore a thick, cornified pad and sheath, representing a unique integumentary feature not seen in other species.
This feature was likely used for locking and pushing in intraspecific combat, similar to muskoxen.
The presence of skeletons ranging from juveniles to adults in the Pipestone Creek bonebed suggests that Pachyrhinosaurus cared for its young.
Growth was rapid; P. perotorum reached 28 percent of its adult body size by the age of one year and was nearly half the size of a mature adult by the age of two.
The genus Pachyrhinosaurus is integrated within the subfamily Centrosaurinae inside the family Ceratopsidae.
Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai lived from about 73.5 to 72.5 million years ago.
Fossils from the St. Mary River Formation range geographically from Glacier County, Montana, to the Little Bow River in Alberta.
The Horseshoe Canyon Formation, another source of Pachyrhinosaurus fossils, has been dated between 74 and 67 million years old.
In the Prince Creek Formation, P. perotorum engaged in niche partitioning with Edmontosaurus, preferring upland environments while the latter favored lowland deltas.

In the ecosystem of the St. Mary River Formation, the tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus was likely the apex predator alongside Pachyrhinosaurus, while in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, the tyrannosaurid Albertosaurus sarcophagus was the apex predator of the paleoenvironment.
In the Horseshoe Canyon Formation, hadrosaurs dominated the dinosaur population, making up half of all dinosaurs in the region.

It was previously thought that P. perotorum had unique forward-projecting horns, but 2019 research showed these were inaccurately reconstructed and it actually had backward-pointing horns like its sister species.
Scientists are not very sure if it had a nasal horn because no complete skulls have been found.
